channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Lula e Flávio fazem guerra de preços de comida nas redes sociais
item.description: The Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) campaigns are clashing on social media over basic food prices, using videos and posts to criticize or counter inflation narratives. The battle centers on economic issues, with both sides selectively highlighting data to attack each other.

item.title: De PL a PCO: 51 candidatos a governo já criticaram o STF ou pediram impeachment de Moraes
item.description: 51 out of 194 2026 gubernatorial candidates have criticized the STF or called for Moraes' impeachment, including names from PL and PCO. PCO leads with 18 critical candidates, followed by PL with 10. These criticisms aim to attract Bolsonaro voters and question the alleged judicial dictatorship in Brazil.

item.title: Lula divide chapas ao Senado com 10 governadores, e Flávio, com 6; veja os cenários em cada Estado
item.description: The 2026 elections are set to intensify polarization in the Senate, with Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro dividing slates across dozens of states. While Lula has backing from governors, mainly in the Northeast, Flávio leads numerically with more endorsed candidates. The alliances reflect the fragmentation of the national political landscape.

item.title: Band e ‘Estadão’ promovem primeiro debate entre os candidatos a presidente em 2026; saiba como será
item.description: Grupo Bandeirantes and Estadão host the first 2026 presidential debate with four confirmed candidates, while Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro are absent. The debate will be streamed live at 8 PM on Estadão’s digital platforms. The forum gains prominence due to low voter recognition of candidates and the absence of leading figures.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro cria comissão evangélica para organizar ato do 7 de Setembro na Paulista
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) formed an evangelical commission to organize the September 7th parade on Paulista Avenue, aiming to rally popular support after the underwhelming turnout at the campaign kickoff event in Copacabana.

item.title: Erosão democrática: a presença das organizações criminosas nas eleições
item.description: The article examines how criminal organizations influence electoral processes in Latin America through illegal funding, corruption, and territorial control to condition democratic outcomes. Cases like Mexico illustrate the complexity of the relationship between illicit economies and politics, particularly in Brazil, where the reach of these organizations exacerbates democratic erosion.

item.title: Marçal promete recuar de candidatura se não tiver segurança jurídica
item.description: Pablo Marçal (PRTB) states he will not run for the Planalto Palace in 2026 unless his candidacy is judicially approved, avoiding harm to Lula in the first round. He could aid Lula by drawing votes from Flávio Bolsonaro, but his sub-judice candidacy may be annulled post-election, reducing valid votes.

item.title: Planalto vê abertura com Trump para renegociar tarifaço após eleição
item.description: The Brazilian government moves forward in renegotiating U.S. tariffs after the phone call between Lula and Trump, which reopened commercial dialogue. A meeting between trade representatives of both countries is scheduled for next week to discuss the 25% and 12.5% rates on Brazilian exports. The resumption of talks follows months of deadlock and increased tensions between the governments.

item.title: Dois filhos (Lulinha e Flávio Bolsonaro), dois pesos e duas medidas
item.description: The article contrasts Fábio Lula (Lulinha), whose record is free of business deals or candidacies, with Flávio Bolsonaro, accused of not explaining the whereabouts of R$ 61 million received for a film about Jair Bolsonaro. It criticizes media bias and questions the focus on Lulinha to attack Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. Flávio, son of a former president, remains silent on the case for 100 days, while Lulinha avoids controversies.

item.title: Irregularidades em adesivos eleitorais é a 3ª mais denunciada no DF
item.description: Reports of irregular electoral stickers in DF account for 18.6% of national occurrences, with 12 records in the first six days of campaigning. The practice, though common, must follow TSE rules such as a 0.5m² limit and prohibition in service vehicles.

item.title: Band promove 1º debate presidencial neste domingo. Veja quem participa
item.description: Band hosts the first 2026 presidential debate with Caiado, Zema, Renan and Cury; Lula, Flávio and Marçal are absent.

item.title: Eleições 2026: mais de 6.900 candidatos não declararam bens
item.description: TSE data reveals that 6,933 out of 20,682 candidates in the 2026 elections did not declare assets to the electoral court, accounting for 33.56% of all candidacies. Some candidates declared negligible assets, such as R$0.01, mostly linked to checking account deposits.

item.title: "Bilionários por engano": saiba quem são os candidatos que erraram registro
item.description: Three candidates in the 2026 elections declared billions of assets to the TSE but later claimed typographical errors. Pablo Marçal (PRTB) corrected from R$7.4 billion to R$149.9 million; Maria Lúcia Soares Viana (PSol-TO) corrected from R$2.07 billion to approximately R$2 million; and Dr. Giorgia Michelleti (PSDB-AC) corrected a house from R$1.1 billion to R$1.1 million. Their teams confirmed the discrepancies were due to mixing up thousands and millions.

item.title: Veja a agenda dos candidatos ao governo de SP neste domingo (23/8)
item.description: This Sunday (August 23rd) marks one week into the São Paulo gubernatorial race, with seven candidates competing for the seat. Tarcísio de Freitas and Fernando Haddad lead the polls, followed by Vera Lúcia, Carlos Machado, Izadora Dias, Policial Edjane, and Vivian Mendes. Each candidate has scheduled campaign events and activities for the day.

item.title: Bolsonarinho, Lulinha e o efeito do prestígio de Lula na eleição
item.description: Datafolha survey shows Lula's significant lead over Bolsonaro, contradicting rumors of a tight race. Lula's prestige may influence undecided voters in the 2026 election.

item.title: Federações partidárias neutras na corrida presidencial reúnem 3,7 mil candidatos nas eleições
item.description: Five neutral party federations fielded 3,766 candidates in the 2026 elections, focusing on contests for the National Congress due to Federal Party Fund resources. Only the PT, PCdoB and PV Federation led by Lula and the PSol and REDE alliance declared support for a presidential candidate, while others remained neutral, including União Brasil and Progressistas.

item.title: Mais de 900 candidatos mudaram declaração de cor ou raça no TSE entre 2022 e 2026
item.description: Between 2022 and 2026, 909 candidates who previously ran changed their declared race or color in the TSE, accounting for 14.4% of the 6,315 who kept the same profile. The most common shift was from brown (parda) to white (branca), with 322 cases, followed by white to brown, with 317. However, specialists emphasize that these changes alone do not confirm misconduct, as factors like identity perception, administrative errors, or party mediation may play a role.

item.title: Eleições 2026: 404 candidatos usam títulos religiosos em nome de urna
item.description: TSE data reveals that 404 candidates in the 2026 elections used religious titles on the ballot name, such as pastor, brother, or priestess, concentrated mainly in legislative races. Religion is leveraged as a political agenda and electoral platform, reflecting demand for faith-based proposals. The phenomenon also includes figures like Michelle Bolsonaro, who, though evangelical, did not adopt a religious title on the ballot.

item.title: VÍDEO: Influenciador pode fazer campanha eleitoral?
item.description: Digital influencers can express their political opinions on social media, but they cannot receive financial benefits or promote content in a paid manner. The TSE banned practices like 'cutting contests', which pay creators to spread campaign content. The g1 series explains how new technologies impact the 2026 elections.

item.title: Na Festa de Barretos, Flávio diz que vai "resgatar" agro brasileiro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro used the Barretos rodeo festival to defend agribusiness, claiming he will 'recover' the sector. He was accompanied by Tarcísio de Freitas and other right-wing politicians. He also declared war on 'drug traffickers' starting January 2026.

item.title: PF vê plano de amiga de Lulinha para conta fora do Brasil, diz revista
item.description: The Brazilian Federal Police is investigating plans by Roberta Luchsinger, a friend of Fábio Lula (Lulinha), to open a bank account and company in Liechtenstein, suspected of hiding illicit funds. Investigations also reveal cash usage and instructions to conceal sums in suitcases and wardrobes. Luchsinger and Lulinha face probes at the Supreme Court on suspicion of corruption and money laundering.

item.title: Lula tem 60% dos votos no 1º turno no Piauí, diz Datafolha
item.description: A Datafolha poll released on August 22, 2026, shows President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) leading voter intentions in Piauí with 60% in the first round. In a potential runoff, Lula reaches 68% against 24% for Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ). The survey was conducted between August 18 and 21, 2026, with a margin of error of ±3 percentage points and 95% confidence level.

item.title: Eleição presidencial tem primeiro debate com provável ausência de Lula e Flávio
item.description: The first presidential debate of 2026 takes place without the presence of Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, allowing other candidates to increase their visibility. The event, promoted by Grupo Bandeirantes, occurs this Sunday at 8 PM.

item.title: 2º turno em SP: Flávio tem 47% contra 42% de Lula, mostra Datafolha
item.description: A Datafolha poll shows Flávio Bolsonaro leading with 47% of voting intentions against Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's 42% in a potential second round in São Paulo, with a 2-point margin of error. In Minas Gerais, the candidates are tied technically, with Lula ahead by 46% to 42%, within the 3-point margin of error. Both polls, filed with the Electoral Court, indicate recent stability in voter intentions in the country's largest electoral colleges.

item.title: Datafolha: no Piauí, Lula marca 68% contra 24% de Flávio em 2º turno
item.description: Datafolha poll in Piauí shows Lula leading with 68% against Flávio Bolsonaro's 24% in a potential runoff. In the first round, Lula leads with 60%, followed by Flávio with 19%.

item.title: Ala do PSol é barrada em ato de Lula e Paes no Rio de Janeiro
item.description: PSol members were blocked by Eduardo Paes from participating in the campaign event with Lula in Rio. The decision followed PSol launching its own candidates, creating tension with the PT alliance. Despite the barrier, PSol lawmakers and candidates remained present at the event.

item.title: Datafolha: Lula lidera em PE e PI, e Flávio aparece à frente em SP, RJ e DF; em Minas, há empate técnico
item.description: A Datafolha survey released on Saturday shows Lula leading in Pernambuco and Piauí and tied technically in Minas Gerais in a second-round scenario, while Flávio Bolsonaro leads in São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro and the Federal District. In Minas, considered a decisive state, the technical tie occurs with 46% for Lula and 42% for Flávio, within the three-point margin of error. The survey, conducted last week, has a margin of error of two to three percentage points.

item.title: Datafolha: Lula tem 46% de avaliação positiva em PE e 27% em SP e RJ
item.description: The latest Datafolha poll shows President Lula with 46% positive approval in Pernambuco, the highest among the five states surveyed. In São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro, approval drops to 27%, while the Federal District leads with 51% negative ratings. The survey also highlights Minas Gerais as a strategic state in the presidential race.

item.title: A vantagem aberta por Flávio Bolsonaro sobre Lula no Rio e no DF, segundo o Datafolha
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) leads vot intentions over Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) in both the Federal District and Rio de Janeiro, according to Datafolha polls. In a second-round scenario, the senator reaches 51% against 39% in the DF and 49% against 40% in Rio, with margins exceeding the margin of error. Furthermore, approval of the Lula government is in the minority in both states.

item.title: Os estados em que Lula tem mais de 30 pontos de vantagem sobre Flávio, segundo o Datafolha
item.description: Datafolha polls show President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) leading by over 30 percentage points against Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) in both Pernambuco and Piauí, especially in hypothetical runoff scenarios. In Pernambuco, Lula holds 62% of voter intentions versus 29% for Flávio, while in Piauí the gap is wider at 68% to 24%. Additionally, Lula’s administration enjoys majority approval in both states, indicating a favorable political climate for the PT in the Northeast.

item.title: Tarcísio: operações de crédito do Amapá não ficam travadas; de SP, ficam
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas defended the formation of a strong center-right bloc in the Senate and claimed that São Paulo is poorly represented in the House. Without mentioning Davi Alcolumbre, the governor compared Amapá, saying that credit operations from the state are not stalled like those of São Paulo.

item.title: Datafolha: Flávio Bolsonaro lidera disputa presidencial no DF
item.description: A Datafolha poll released on August 22nd shows Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) leading the presidential race among voters in the Federal District, with 39% of voting intentions, followed by Lula (PT) with 31% and Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) with 10%. In a scenario including Pablo Marçal (PRTB), Flávio has 37% and Lula maintains 31%, indicating that his inclusion does not significantly change the overall picture. The margin of error is three percentage points, with a 95% confidence level.

item.title: Eleições 2026: veja como está a corrida presidencial em SP, RJ, DF, MG, PE e PI, segundo o Datafolha
item.description: Datafolha polls released this Saturday (22) show the presidential race split across six Brazilian states. Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) leads in São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, and the Federal District, while Lula (PT) is ahead in Pernambuco, Minas Gerais, and Piauí. In São Paulo, Flávio has 37% versus Lula's 33%, with Renan Santos (Missão) in third at 5%.

item.title: No RJ, Flávio marca 49% contra 40% de Lula em 2º turno, diz Datafolha
item.description: Datafolha poll shows Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) leading with 49% against Lula's (PT) 40% in a potential runoff in Rio de Janeiro. In the first round, Flávio leads 41% to 36%. Survey of 1,204 voters conducted Aug 18-20, with a 3-point margin of error.

item.title: Datafolha: veja os índices de popularidade de Lula em São Paulo, Minas, Rio, Pernambuco e DF
item.description: A Datafolha poll released on August 22, 2026, 43 days before the first round, shows Lula's decline in popularity in São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, and the Federal District, where negative ratings exceed positive ones. In Minas Gerais the gap is narrower, while in Pernambuco the president enjoys majority approval. Nationally, Lula leads with 39% versus Flávio Bolsonaro's 33%, and would win a runoff 47% to 43%.

item.title: Kassab caminha para Lula no segundo turno, mas escorrega na lama do Lulinha
item.description: Kassab and the PSD are moving toward pro-Lula neutrality in the runoff, leveraging Caiado's 5% as bargaining power. According to Datafolha, Flávio Bolsonaro remains competitive against Lula (43% to 47%), while Caiado trails. The scenario, however, is volatile and could shift due to scandals involving Lulinha and lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger, which threaten the Bolsonaro ticket.

item.title: Datafolha mostra rejeição a Lula nos maiores colégios eleitorais
item.description: A Datafolha poll shows strong rejection of Lula's government in Brazil's largest electoral strongholds. In São Paulo, 48% rate the administration as bad or very bad, compared to 27% who consider it great or good, posing one of the main challenges to the president's reelection bid.

item.title: Lula tem 62% e Flávio, 29%, no 2º turno em PE, diz Datafolha
item.description: A Datafolha poll in Pernambuco shows Lula (PT) with a wide lead in the 2nd round, reaching 62% of voter intentions against 29% for Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). In the 1st round scenarios, Lula ranges between 55% and 56%, while Flávio remains at 24%, indicating strong polarization and the president's dominance in the state.

item.title: Datafolha: Lula tem 62% e Flávio 29% em Pernambuco no 2º turno
item.description: A Datafolha poll released on August 22 shows Lula (PT) with 62% versus 29% for Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) in a hypothetical runoff in Pernambuco, a 33-point lead. In the first round, Lula leads with 56% (without Marçal) or 55% (with Marçal), followed by Flávio at 24% in both scenarios. The survey interviewed 1,204 voters with a margin of error of three percentage points.

item.title: Rafael Fonteles tem 56% e venceria no 1º turno no Piauí, diz Datafolha
item.description: A Datafolha poll released on August 22, 2026, shows Piauí Governor Rafael Fonteles (PT) would win the state gubernatorial election in the first round with 56% of voting intentions. Joel Rodrigues (PP) is in second place with 21%, followed by several candidates with marginal percentages (1% to 2%). Blank/null votes account for 10%, and 5% of respondents did not know or did not answer. The survey interviewed 826 people, has a margin of error of 3 percentage points, and is registered with Brazil's Superior Electoral Court (TSE).

item.title: Lula tem 46% e Flávio 42% no 2º turno em MG, diz Datafolha
item.description: Datafolha poll released on Aug 22, 2026 shows a technical tie in Minas Gerais between Lula (46%) and Flávio Bolsonaro (42%) in a potential runoff, within the 3-point margin of error. In the first round, Lula leads with 37%, followed by Flávio (31%) and Zema (10%); a scenario including Pablo Marçal keeps Lula ahead at 36%.

item.title: Caiado muda de posição e diz ser a favor do fim da escala 6x1
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), a presidential candidate, reversed his position on ending the 6x1 work schedule and declared himself in favor of the proposal during an event in Campinas, just three days after dismissing it as 'populist' and 'electioneering'. At the press conference he also called debate-avoiding rivals 'runaways'—without naming Lula or Flávio Bolsonaro—proposed a new crime category called 'domestic terrorism,' and pledged to build 40 maximum-security prisons with expanded use of artificial intelligence.

item.title: Datafolha: Flávio marca 47% contra 42% de Lula em SP no 2º turno; MG tem empate
item.description: A Datafolha poll shows Flávio Bolsonaro leading in São Paulo in a runoff with 47% versus Lula's 42%, a state representing 21% of Brazil's electorate. In Minas Gerais, there is a technical tie: Lula scores 46% and Flávio 42%, within the three-point margin of error. At the state level, Tarcísio leads in SP and Cleitinho Azevedo leads in MG.

item.title: Flávio tem 49% e Lula, 40%, no 2º turno no RJ, diz Datafolha
item.description: A Datafolha poll released on August 22, 2026, shows Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) leading President Lula (PT) in a hypothetical 2nd round in Rio de Janeiro, with 49% versus 40%. In the 1st round, Flávio leads with 38% (with Pablo Marçal) or 41% (without Marçal), while Lula has 37% or 36%, respectively. The survey interviewed 1,204 voters, has a margin of error of 3 percentage points, and is registered with the TSE under number BR-08448/2026.

item.title: Cleitinho pede que PT não puna prefeita em MG que deseja apoiá-lo
item.description: Cleitinho Azevedo (Republicanos), candidate for governor of Minas Gerais, defended Mayor Jackeliny Nascimento of Frei Gaspar (PT), who publicly endorsed his campaign despite her party affiliation. The gesture could be considered party disloyalty, and the state PT directory, led by deputy Leninha, will review possible penalties. Cleitinho asked the PT not to punish the mayor and highlighted a parliamentary amendment he allocated to the municipality.

item.title: Filha do ministro aposentado do STF Ayres Britto se casa
item.description: Lawyer Nara Pinheiro Reis Ayres Britto, daughter of retired Supreme Court Justice Carlos Ayres Britto, married fellow attorney Bryan de Jongh Martins; both are partners at the Ayres Britto law firm founded by her father. Carlos Ayres Britto served on the Supreme Court from 2003 to 2012, was appointed by President Lula, presided over the Court and the Electoral Tribunal, and retired upon reaching the mandatory age of 70.

item.title: Lulinha planejou viagem para África e Europa com lobista, diz revista
item.description: A Veja magazine report revealed that messages recovered by the Federal Police show Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, known as Lulinha, and lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger planning trips to Africa and Paris in 2024, with an estimated cost of US$ 20,000 per person. In the messages, Luchsinger states she was researching the travel costs. The case involves indications of lobbying ties with the son of President Lula.

item.title: Datafolha: A vantagem de Flávio Bolsonaro sobre Lula no maior colégio eleitoral do país
item.description: A Datafolha poll conducted between August 18 and 21 in São Paulo shows Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) numerically ahead of Lula in the state: 37% to 33% in the first round and 47% to 42% in a hypothetical runoff, with the gap falling inside or outside the margin of error depending on the scenario. With Pablo Marçal included in the first round, Flávio and Lula are technically tied (35% to 34%). Lula's government is rated bad or very bad by 48% of São Paulo voters, while 27% rate it good or very good and 24% consider it average.

item.title: Flávio tem 51% e Lula, 39%, no 2º turno no DF, diz Datafolha
item.description: A Datafolha poll released on August 22, 2026 shows Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) leading President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) 51% to 39% in a hypothetical 2nd round for the Presidency among voters in Brazil's Federal District. Blank/null votes total 9% and undecided voters 2%. In the 1st round, Flávio has 37% (or 39% without Pablo Marçal) and Lula 31%, followed by Ronaldo Caiado (9-10%). The survey interviewed 910 voters, with a 3-point margin of error and 95% confidence level.

item.title: Caiado chama de ‘fujões’ adversários que devem faltar a debates
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) called potential debate absentees "fugitives," claiming those who avoid debates shouldn't even be allowed to register their candidacies. Romeu Zema (Novo) advocated for a new pension reform with contribution periods tied to life expectancy. Renan Santos (Missão) promised a "National Slum Eradication Framework" requiring an estimated R$1.3 to R$1.5 trillion over 10-15 years.
